definition: The scale space representation of a signal obtained by Gaussian smoothing satisfies a number of special properties, scale-space axioms, which make it into a special form of multi-scale representation.
details: There are, however, also other types of "multi-scale approaches" in the areas of computer vision, image processing and signal processing, in particular the notion of wavelets. The purpose of this article is to describe a few of these approaches:

explainer.lead: Multi-scale approaches examine an image or signal at several levels of detail, from fine local variations to broader structures. They matter because a pattern that is hard to interpret at one scale may become clear at another.

tiers.eli5: It is like looking at a drawing both up close and from far away: up close you see tiny lines, while from farther away you see the whole shape. Multi-scale approaches let a computer use both views instead of choosing just one.
tiers.practitioner: In computer vision, image processing, and signal processing, apply Gaussian smoothing across scales to build a scale-space representation, or use wavelets as another multi-scale approach. Choose the scale range to match the details of interest, and remember that smoothing changes the signal rather than merely displaying it at different sizes.
tiers.paperLevel: For a signal f, Gaussian scale space can be written L(·; s) = G_s * f, where G_s is a Gaussian kernel parameterized by scale s and * denotes convolution. This representation satisfies scale-space axioms that make it a special form of multi-scale representation; wavelets provide a different type of multi-scale approach.

explainer.example: For an image containing a small mark on a larger object, fine scales preserve the mark while stronger Gaussian smoothing emphasizes the object's broader shape. The resulting scale-space representation lets both structures be examined instead of forcing one scale to serve both purposes.

usedIn.detail: Represents visual structures across different levels of detail.

usedIn.name: Image processing
usedIn.detail: Uses Gaussian smoothing or wavelets to analyze image content at multiple scales.

usedIn.name: Signal processing
usedIn.detail: Examines both fine variations and broader structure in a signal.

explainer.intuition: A single view can mix small details with large structures. Looking across scales separates these levels of detail so each can be examined in a more useful way.
howItWorks: Start with an image or other signal.
Analyze it at several scales rather than only its original resolution of detail.
For scale space, apply Gaussian smoothing with different scale parameters.
Alternatively, use wavelets to obtain another kind of multi-scale representation.
Interpret fine-scale and coarse-scale information together.
explainer.whyItMatters: Images and signals contain structure at more than one scale, so a single-scale description can miss either small details or broader patterns. Multi-scale representations provide a principled way to retain and analyze these different views.
misconceptions: Gaussian scale space is not the only multi-scale approach; wavelets are another important type.
A multi-scale representation is not just one smoothed result: it represents the signal across multiple scales.
